title: Activation choreography and anti-oscillation protocol (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for activating features across cohorts with an explicit anti-oscillation layer. Intended audience: product PMs, release engineers, SREs, and rollout stewards.

TL;DR:
- Define precise signal windowing and hysteresis for each gate (not just a single threshold).
- Never flip cohorts faster than a configured cool-down.
- Use synthetic probes + live telemetry to detect emergent oscillation patterns early.
- Pre-wire a "soft-revert" path (route -> lower-cost model or limited-capacity variant) before a hard rollback.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to multi-model/hybrid routing experiments (hosted + dedicated variants), latency-sensitive features, and reranking/chat features where small drift has outsized UX impact.
- Assumes telemetry into Console dashboards (per-model latency, error rate, token-per-call cost, UXR signals) and a routable traffic switch that supports slice-level weights.

Quick glossary (local terms used below):
- steward: person responsible for the activation window (ops oncall or release PM).
- slice: a user cohort or traffic partition (region, percent, feature-flag bucket).
- oscillation: rapid toggle between states causing instability or thrashing (e.g., toggling model A/B back and forth).

Roles & routines (skeleton):
- Activation owner (PM) — defines hypothesis, primary UX metrics, tolerance windows.
- Steward (ops/release engineer) — runs the activation command, monitors signals, executes reversion if needed.
- SRE oncall — ready to respond for infra anomalies; paged on defined infra thresholds.
- Data analyst — runs quick post-activation checks (stat checks, drift).
- UX lead — available for customer-impact triage.

Suggested pre-activation checklist (quick):
- [ ] Hypothesis documented in experiment canvas (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Canary traffic slice(s) defined and registered with Console.
- [ ] Observability dashboard runbook: latency, 95/99 p50/p90/p99, error types, user success rate, cost-per-1000-tokens.
- [ ] Synthetic probe test cases uploaded and smoke-passed in sandbox.
- [ ] Revert plan written: soft-fallback variant + hard rollback steps.
- [ ] Stakeholder sync time and on-call rotation published.

Signal definitions and gating heuristics (examples):
- Latency (model-serving p99): gate if p99 increases > 30% and absolute increase > 150ms sustained for 10m window AND trend is monotonic over last three 5m buckets.
- Error rate (5xx or inference aborts): gate if rate > 0.5% of traffic for >= 5m and correlated with CPU/GPU saturation alerts.
- Cost-per-call: gate if unit-cost increases > 20% and predicted monthly runcost > budgeted delta.
- Quality (UX metric): gate if top-level success metric — e.g., rerank CTR or accept-rate — drops by > 2% absolute or >10% relative with p<0.05 over A/B test window.
- Manual stop: any verified user-visible safety incident or clear hallucination spike — immediate stop.

Anti-oscillation strategies (core principles):
1) Hysteresis windows — require both entry and exit conditions. For example: to move from 5% -> 25% we require 20m of healthy signals; to revert we require 5m of negative signal sustained plus at least 10m cool-down since last weight change.
2) Minimum dwell time — every cohort weight change must be followed by a minimum dwell time (suggested default = 15m for latency-sensitive features, 60m for large A/Bs).
3) Exponential backoff on re-tries — if a change triggers a revert, next attempt must wait longer (e.g., 15m -> 45m -> 120m) and require manual steward approval after 2 fails.
4) Rate-limited switches — only allow X% traffic change per step (e.g., +10% per step) to avoid abrupt capacity shocks.
5) Soft fallback path — route to a compatible lower-risk variant while leaving the higher-risk route in a parked state (helps preserve cache-warmth & avoids immediate oscillation).
6) Synthetic-probe-driven gate overrides — prioritize probe failures for safety, but require human confirmation for non-synthetic anomalies.

Activation choreography (step-by-step example for a typical microcanary):
0) Prechecks done and stakeholders in Slack channel #release-activation.
1) Start with slice A = 1% traffic (synthetic included) -> record baseline for 20m. Steward starts a short observation timer.
2) After 20m healthy: step to 5% (+4%) in one atomic command. Wait min dwell time (15m) and watch signals.
3) If stable, step to 15% after synthetic probes run and data analyst validates. Dwell = 30m.
4) If any gate trips, perform soft fallback (route affected slice to fallback variant) then open a postmortem thread; do not automatically toggle back to prior state until postmortem.
5) After reaching target exposure (e.g., 50%): run last 2-3 larger-scale synthetic sweeps and ramp to 100% with larger dwell windows and cost review.

Communication patterns (templates):
- Slack ephemeral to #release-activation: "[steward] starting step -> slice=web-ff-7 -> 1% -> expected dwell=20m. Monitoring p99/err/cost. Ping @sre-oncall if infra alarms"
- Quick incident page: short facts, impact, immediate actions, revert state, who paged.

Synthetic probe design notes (short):
- Probes should hit representative prompt distributions (short/medium/long tokens). Include edge-case prompts that historically surface hallucinations.
- Maintain a small bank of golden-responses for deterministic parts of the pipeline (rerank consistency checks, fallback detection).
- Run probes at 5x amplification to increase signal visibility during low-traffic windows.

Reversion and recovery steps (practical):
- Soft-fallback command (preferred): route slice -> model-variant:stable-v2 while keeping telemetry. Notify stakeholders and tag the experiment.
- Hard rollback (if soft-fallback unavailable): route-all -> previous-production and freeze experiment. Launch postmortem.
- Recovery checklist: cache warm-up plan, capacity ramp, telemetry sanity, customer communications.

Metrics to capture in every activation event (minimum):
- pre/post differences for p50/p90/p99 latency, error rate, cost-per-1k-tokens, top UX metric.
- timestamped event log of weight changes + steward id + reason.
- synthetic probe pass/fail counts.

Observability recommendations (console wiring):
- Attach a single experiment id to all traces and logs.
- Dashboard with small multiples: per-slice metrics side-by-side.
- Auto-bake quick stat tests (t-tests/bootstrapped CI) for key UX metrics, surfaced as green/amber/red.

When to escalate to page (suggested thresholds):
- infra saturation alerts (GPU memory, CPU steal) correlated with increased p99 by >40%
- sustained 5xx >1% for 10m with rising trend
- any verified safety/user complaint with severity > high

Open questions / TODOs (triage this list):
- (TODO) Define default dwell times per product vertical (chat vs embeddings vs rerank).
- (Q) Should we allow an automated revert for cost-only gates? risk: flip-flop when autoscaler spikes.
- (TODO) Add explicit CLI commands in release repo: start-step, step-up, soft-fallback, freeze-experiment. (see PR linked_artifacts)
- (Q) How do we best capture and visualize hysteresis in Console? small-time-series widget or discrete event timeline?

Appendix: simple steward checklist (copyable)
- Confirm experiment id + stakeholders
- Run smoke probes and confirm pass
- Start at initial slice -> note timestamp + steward handles
- Observe dwell -> record metrics at 5/15/30m buckets
- Step only if all green and no infra alarms
- On any gate: execute soft-fallback and open postmortem thread

Notes to self / rough thoughts (scratch):
- felt uneasy about purely automated reverts. In practice, human confirmation for user-visible failures saves churn.
- idea: a "parked" state that preserves warm caches but prevents traffic until steward approves; could reduce thrash.
- possibility: attach a patience score (composite of short-term and mid-term signals) and require patience>threshold to proceed.

History / provenance:
